what_happened: The person running Athena edited athena.toml directly in the shared working copy while a batch was running. The first commit of the edit was refused, so the file stayed uncommitted for a few minutes. During that time a landing's self-rebuild needed a clean tree, refused to build from the dirty one, and the batch stopped. No job is recorded as failed. The person did not stage the change with `athena intervene --with-staged` and did not check whether a landing was due.
cause: The shared working copy is used by the running batch, and Athena does not guard it against hand edits. Nothing stops or warns about an uncommitted change to a governed file while a drain is active. Nothing shows that a landing's self-rebuild is due and needs a clean tree. The safe route (`athena intervene --with-staged`) is only a convention the person has to remember. Any in-place edit that is not committed at once can therefore collide with a rebuild, and the batch stops.
other_causes: The first commit was refused (the reason is not given), which stretched the dirty window from seconds to minutes.
The drain's self-rebuild stops on a dirty tree instead of waiting or reporting which file is dirty.
open_hypotheses: Why the first commit was refused is not stated. If a policy or test check refused it, the edit may have been wrong as well as mistimed.
The input does not say whether the drain could have resumed on its own once the tree was clean.
prevention: Add a code check that, while a drain is running, refuses or warns on hand commands and edits that leave the shared working tree dirty. Have it point to `athena intervene --with-staged`. Have the landing's self-rebuild report which files are dirty and wait briefly, instead of stopping the batch at once. The same check covers other hand commands that write into the shared tree during a landing, such as claim renewal.
proposed_request: Make Athena protect the shared working copy while a drain is running. (1) Add a guard so that when a drain is active, `athena` hand commands that write into the shared working tree, and a dirty tracked file such as athena.toml found at a landing's self-rebuild, are detected. Print a clear message that names the dirty files and says to use `athena intervene --with-staged` instead. (2) Make the landing's self-rebuild wait up to a short, configurable time for the tree to become clean before it refuses. If it still refuses, record the dirty file names in the drain's stop reason. Acceptance: a test with a dirty athena.toml during a landing rebuild shows the message and the recorded reason. A test where the tree is cleaned within the wait shows the batch continuing without a stop. Add the CHANGELOG.md entry.
